newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens vs dlr as demand rises.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens vs dlr as demand rises.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened against the dollar on Wednesday on increased dollar demand from the interbank market, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.57 against the dollar from 53.51 on Tuesday, while against the pound it was posted at 88.72 from 87.82.
"The market definitely moved today. We've seen a depreciation of the shilling," one dealer said.
"There's a lot of demand from people who wanted to cover their short positions," another dealer told Reuters.
At midday, dealers said they were trading at 53.63/78 from the day's opening.
However some dealers said rumours of dollar inflows from foreign investors could check the shilling's bearish sentiment.
Meanwhile the money market remained slightly illiquid with overnight rates quoted at 17 percent from Tuesday's 16-18 percent.
